scope: All 34 v2 contact sheets and their 340 frame positions; all 25 mask-changed frames enlarged; all 11 prior failed frames and all 3 prior uncertainty observations rechecked.
method: Actually opened all34 contact.png with view_image detail=original and compared source, skin/hair overlay, and tint at all10 frame positions.
Opened all25 mask-changed audit.png panels plus two unchanged ponytail uncertainty panels; additionally opened four masks.png panels for suspected source boundaries.
Recorded visual findings before reading exact pixel values. Numerical reads corroborate observed regions; no classifier, box coverage, or image count establishes semantic correctness.
Compared all272 S/idle masks and variants byte-for-byte with frozen live references. This is a separate mechanical identity result.
coordinate_note: Exact points are zero-based original-source x,y. Approximate bboxes use half-open [left,top,right,bottom] and are location aids, not authored annotation polygons.
broad_contact_limit: Two substantial arm omissions were identified only in enlarged panels. Therefore contact-sheet coverage is explicitly not evidence of exhaustive pixel-level semantic accuracy.

display_erratum.effect: The diagnostic display title is stale. Image files were not relabeled during this review; hashes bind the actually viewed pixels. Final S/idle anchor identity was checked separately below.

mechanical_frozen_reference_check.semantic_claim: NONE: equality to the frozen references does not prove correct masks.

limits: V1 FAIL and v2 FAIL are both retained; repaired prior defects do not erase the newly observed v2 failures.
This broader corpus review does not replace the separate strict40-frame hair50/coverage audit.
No full pixel accuracy, formal hair silhouette percentage, runtime acceptance, generated-portrait inspection, blind-review participation, integration acceptance, or owner approval is claimed.
Dark hair/protected ink and narrow source boundaries remain UNCERTAIN rather than being forced to PASS.
The exact11 former defects are visually resolved; that statement is deliberately narrower than whole-corpus acceptance.

findings.description: Most of the plainly exposed upper arm and forearm remain unselected and orange in the light tint. Only a tiny wrist patch is selected. This was found by enlarging the changed frame; the broad contact screen missed it.

The image-left supporting arm remains almost wholly unselected and orange, while the opposite arm is lightened. The region is small in absolute pixels but comprises most of the visibly exposed near arm. This was found in the last changed-frame enlargement after the broad contact screen.

The rear/lower ponytail stays dark while the scalp becomes grey. Some ponytail interior is selected, but a dark lower patch remains unchanged. The same source ambiguity remains on the v2 enlarged panel.
findings.source_specific_uncertainty: The unselected patch is very dark and partly translucent at its edge. It may belong to intentionally protected ink/outline. The broad visual review cannot decide whether this is excessive hair omission or establish the formal 50 percent silhouette gate.

findings.description: Most of the small ponytail behind the raised arm remains dark while the main hair cap changes color. The same source ambiguity remains on the v2 enlarged panel.
findings.source_specific_uncertainty: The ponytail is small, dark, and partly overlaps the raised arm/axe area. Source colors alone do not establish whether the remaining dark pixels should be tintable hair or protected ink. No formal hair-coverage verdict is made.

findings.description: A thin selected vertical strip follows the image-right torso/garment seam below the arm. The same source ambiguity remains on the v2 enlarged panel.
findings.source_specific_uncertainty: The source is too ambiguous at this narrow seam to distinguish a small exposed-skin strip from hide trim confidently. Recorded for source-only review, not counted as confirmed clothing leakage.

findings.description: An isolated selected skin pixel at (28,59) sits on the image-left hair/log junction. Its source location is not cleanly separable as a visible ear versus wood in these panels.
findings.source_specific_uncertainty: Could be a small visible ear/skin pixel or log leakage. Source-only clarification was requested from the source annotator; no answer was available when this bounded review was recorded. It is not classified as a confirmed new spill.
